primitives.note: Backstab adds bonus physical damage to basic attacks that land from behind, folded into the same attack instance.
Backstab damage is affected by crit modifiers; Deceive's post-invis attack crits for a fixed 160% (200% if a real crit was rolled), overriding the normal crit multiplier.
Deceive arms Shaco's next basic attack (within 0.25s of breaking stealth) with bonus physical damage added to that attack's damage instance.
Deceive's invisibility + blink is the natural opener that sets up the Backstab-empowered first attack; decides how the 15s fight begins.
Backstab and its Q/E riders require attacking the target from behind; a stationary dummy fight must assume whether/for-how-long 'behind' holds.
Jack in the Box's initial cast, Two-Shiv Poison's dagger throw, and Hallucinate's clone-death explosion each deal damage on a fixed trigger.
A sprung Jack in the Box (and each of R's three mini-boxes) auto-fires magic damage every 0.5s for its active window, i.e. a ticking zone.
The trap box, and Hallucinate's clone plus its three deployed mini-boxes, are separate entities dealing part of the total damage.
Two-Shiv Poison's dagger (and its Backstab bonus) deals 1.5x damage if the target is below 30% max health.
The Backstab bonus rider on Two-Shiv Poison only applies while hitting from behind, layering with the execute condition.
Mana costs (40/70-50/75/100) across four abilities on a base mana pool can meaningfully cap casts inside a 15s fight.
Hallucinate is a cast (vanish+clone) with a separate recast (reposition clone) and a separately-timed explosion/mini-box payload on clone death or expiry.
Deceive.CDRefund=2.5 in the bin suggests a cooldown refund, condition and applicability to a dummy kill undocumented on the wiki.

needsBespoke.why: Every damage-relevant part of Shaco's kit (backstab rider, Deceive's empowered/crit attack, Jack in the Box and Hallucinate's mini-boxes as ticking pets, Two-Shiv's execute) maps onto existing primitives. The only friction is real-world doubt (does backstab/positioning persist, does the clone survive to explode) rather than a mechanic the primitive list cannot express.

unsettled.question: Does Hallucinate's clone (and its explosion + 3 mini-boxes) ever pay off within the 15s damage fight, given the clone lives 18s and a stationary, non-retaliating dummy will not kill it early?
options: Assume the clone survives its full 18s and never explodes within the 15s window, so R contributes only whatever the clone's basic attacks (if any) deal, not the explosion/mini-box damage
Assume the simulator force-expires or force-kills the clone during the fight window so the explosion and mini-boxes always resolve and are counted
Exclude R from the damage rotation entirely as not realistically payoff-positive in a 15s single-target dummy fight

unsettled.question: Does Hallucinate's clone auto-attack the dummy during its lifetime (per HallucinateFull.CloneAADamagePercent), functioning as a pet contributing basic-attack damage, or is that value inapplicable outside real combat/player control against a dummy?
options: Clone auto-attacks the dummy like a controllable pet, dealing 60% of Shaco's basic attack damage per hit
Clone does not auto-attack a stationary dummy in this fight construct (matches the bin annotation 'not-in-a-dummy-fight')

unsettled.question: Is the dummy treated as being attacked 'from behind' for the whole fight (so Backstab and its Q/E riders are always active), or only for the single attack immediately following Deceive's blink?
options: Assume permanent backstab positioning for all attacks/E casts throughout the fight (maximizes damage, simplest assumption)
Assume backstab only applies to the one attack empowered by Deceive right after each Q cast, with normal-facing attacks/E casts the rest of the time

unsettled.question: Does Jack in the Box actually spring and start ticking against a stationary target dummy standing in melee range, given the wiki says it springs 'upon enemy contact,' or does it require the dummy to move onto it?
options: Box springs as soon as Shaco or the dummy is within range/contact after the 2s arm time, so W reliably contributes dot damage
Box only springs on genuine movement-based contact and may never trigger against a truly stationary dummy, so W's damage should be counted as unreliable or zero

unsettled.question: For R's single-target mini-box damage (rank 2 value), is the correct base 50 (matching bin HallucinateFull.STBaseDamage=[25/50/75] and the wiki's own arithmetic reading of '{{ap|25 to 75}}' over 3 ranks) or 75 (as recorded in the R ability part's r_3/r_6 base array [25,75,75])?
options: Use 25/50/75 (bin array and correct arithmetic expansion of the wiki template)
Use 25/75/75 as currently recorded in the finished R ability JSON

proposal: Open by casting Q (Deceive) to blink behind the dummy and go invisible, setting up a from-behind position.
Land the Deceive-empowered basic attack immediately as invisibility breaks, which benefits from Q's bonus damage, Backstab's bonus damage, and the guaranteed 160%/200% crit modifier.
Cast E (Two-Shiv Poison) on cooldown (~every 8s) throughout the fight for its magic damage plus, while positioned from behind, its Backstab bonus.
Cast W (Jack in the Box) on cooldown (~every 15s) at the dummy's location to add its AoE/single-target tick damage once armed and sprung.
Fill all remaining time between ability casts with basic attacks against the dummy, maintaining Backstab positioning if assumed to persist.
Re-cast Q again once its (post-effect) cooldown is up to refresh the empowered-attack/backstab-crit window and continue the loop.

Treat R (Hallucinate) as optional/low-priority given its long cooldown (80-100s) and clone lifetime (18s) exceeding the fight duration; cast it only if the sim counts clone auto-attacks or forces the explosion to resolve.
questions: Should R be included in the max-damage rotation for a single 15s dummy fight at all, or is it strictly worse than spending the cast time on Q/E/W and auto-attacks?
Does the simulator model 'attacking from behind' as a toggle the player can hold indefinitely against a stationary dummy, or does it need to be re-earned (e.g. only right after a Deceive blink)?
Is Deceive's cooldown-refund (Deceive.CDRefund) triggered by damaging or killing the dummy, and if so does it apply within this fight?
Does Jack in the Box's spring condition ever trigger in a fight where only Shaco is moving and the dummy stands still?
